prompt:
Research what the Rust project officially documents about its release cadence and how long each stable version is supported. Cite the official Rust page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on my research of the official Rust documentation, here are the findings regarding the release cadence and support window:

The Rust project officially documents a very specific release cadence and support window. Every six weeks, a new stable release is published. Once a new stable version is released, the previous stable version receives no further updates, meaning that each stable version is effectively supported only until the immediate next version is released (a six-week window).

SOURCE: https://forge.rust-lang.org/release/process.html | QUOTE: "Rust releases on a six-week cycle." | CLAIM: The official release cadence of the Rust project is every six weeks.
SOURCE: https://forge.rust-lang.org/release/process.html | QUOTE: "When a new stable release is made, the previous stable release has reached its end of life." | CLAIM: Each stable version is only supported until the next stable version is released (a six-week support window).
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Official documentation stating a specific numerical duration (like "6 weeks") as the explicit support lifespan for stable versions; the project only defines the support end condition relative to the next release's arrival rather than citing a standalone support period length.
